item.title: New species of wild cat discovered for first time in more than a century
item.description: Scientists have discovered a new species of wild cat for the first time in more than a century, a Bolivian researcher says.

item.title: F-16 from Texas crashes in Michigan, evacuation order lifted
item.description: An F-16 fighter jet crashed in Grand Traverse County, Michigan, on Thursday, triggering an evacuation order along part of County Road 633, the county's emergency management said.

item.title: Warren Buffett stepping aside as Berkshire Hathaway chairman
item.description: Warren Buffett is stepping aside as Berkshire Hathaway chairman, he announced in a letter to shareholders Friday.

item.title: Swimmer killed in shark attack in front of horrified beachgoers
item.description: It is the latest in a spate of shark attacks in the country and comes just days after a surfer was bitten in an attack in the same state.

item.title: U.N. experts say U.S. may have committed war crimes with 2 Iran strikes
item.description: U.N.-commissioned rights experts say there are "reasonable grounds" to believe the U.S. committed war crimes with strikes that killed scores of Iranian civilians.

item.title: Sacramento Sikh truck driver survives being stabbed 17 times at Wyoming rest stop
item.description: A Sacramento Sikh truck driver was stabbed 17 times in an unprovoked attack at a Wyoming truck stop on Sunday, his attorney says.

item.title: Family awarded $40 million after daughter left on freeway by Uber driver is killed
item.description: Uber was ordered to pay $40 million to the family of a woman killed on an Orange County freeway after a rideshare driver left her on the side of the road.

item.title: Farmer who voted for Trump says farmers are "all just in survival mode"
item.description: Matt Bell said he initially supported Trump's policies but now feels he and other farmers were "sold a bill of goods" that there was a plan to "put America's farmers and ranchers first."

item.title: Why is a Crystal Lake medical office full of unopened mail, but no employees?
item.description: An unusual charge on an insurance letter led a woman to a bizarre medical office where mountains of unopened mail pile up and no employees have ever been seen.

item.title: Farmer who voted for Trump says "I can't stay in business" amid rising costs
item.description: Matt Bell has been farming in North Carolina for more than half his life. He voted for President Trump but said farmers are "fighting for survival" as they combat rising prices.

item.title: FBI investigation thwarts "mass casualty attack" from man accused of ISIS allegiance
item.description: Federal officials said Jonathan Kramer had armed himself to carry out a mass casualty attack against the American people.

item.title: Holdout juror in Lindsay Clancy trial says he "didn't have any doubts"
item.description: Michael Desronvil, the lone holdout juror in the high-profile Lindsay Clancy murder trial, said he "didn't have any doubts" during deliberations.

item.title: GOP congresswoman says Trump immigration enforcement has "gone too far"
item.description: "The same Hispanics who helped you get to the White House in 2024 feel betrayed," said Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar.

item.title: Legal expert weighs in on Trump's threats to demolish Kennedy Center
item.description: President Trump has suggested that he might demolish the Kennedy Center in Washington, D.C. CBS News legal contributor Jessica Levinson breaks down the constitutional implications.

item.title: Patrick Clancy's wife to appear on 60 Minutes
item.description: Ross Douthat's interview with Patrick Clancy and Dr. Rachel Danis airs Sunday on 60 Minutes.

item.title: Patrick Clancy says he still talks to his kids "all the time"
item.description: This Sunday on 60 Minutes, Patrick Clancy talks about his grief, his memories of his children, and the baseless conspiracy theories that flooded social media since his ex-wife's murder trial.

item.title: Patrick Clancy says he still speaks to his children to "stay connected to them"
item.description: Patrick Clancy and his new wife, fertility doctor Rachel Danis, sat down with 60 Minutes this week. Shanelle Kaul has a preview of the story, which airs Sunday.

item.title: Safe and ethical AI advocate calls international cooperation "absolutely essential"
item.description: OpenAI on Thursday revealed an additional six incidents in which its artificial intelligence models exhibited unexpected or concerning behavior. Stuart Russell, a distinguished professor of computer science at UC Berkeley and president of the International Association for Safe and Ethical AI, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: 1 in 3 Americans with health insurance have medical debt, survey finds
item.description: Nearly half of Americans with medical debt owe at least $2,000, forcing them to make tough choices, new research shows.

item.title: Rep. Rick Larsen says lawmakers "need to get serious" about AI
item.description: From terror groups to possible existential threats to rogue bots, safety concerns over artificial intelligence have grown in recent weeks. Democratic Rep. Rick Larsen of Washington joins CBS News to discuss how Congress can act.

item.title: Week 2 of NFL season kicks off with home opener for Buffalo Bills in new stadium
item.description: The Buffalo Bills kick off Week 2 of the NFL season with a home opener in their new stadium Thursday night. CBS Sports NFL analyst Mike Renner has more.

item.title: What JD Vance's time at Yale says about his transformation from Trump critic to Trump VP
item.description: Chris Whipple, contributing writer at Vanity Fair, joins "The Daily Report" to walk through his reporting on how JD Vance's time at Yale Law may have contributed to his evolution from being an outspoken critic of President Trump to being his vice president.

item.title: Hispanic voters who voted for Trump feel "betrayed," GOP representative says
item.description: Republican Rep. María Elvira Salazar says Hispanic Trump voters are feeling "betrayed" by his immigration crackdown. CBS News' political director Fin Gómez breaks down what this means for midterms.

item.title: Government truck inspections plummeting in many states
item.description: Government roadside inspections of commercial trucks are declining. With that in mind, a CBS News investigation found more than 2,000 people have been killed since 2019 in accidents involving licensed trucking companies that had no roadside inspection on record before the crash. CBS News senior investigative data journalist Steve Reilly reports.

item.title: Experts discuss the potential dangers of AI
item.description: Amid growing concerns about the safety of artificial intelligence following resignations and reports of models going rogue, experts joined CBS News to unpack the potential threat AI could pose to humanity.

item.title: Trump ordered DOJ not to appeal ruling loosening gun limits, sources say
item.description: President Trump ordered the Justice Department not to appeal a court ruling that loosened restrictions on firearms known as "gangster weapons," sources familiar with the matter told CBS News.

item.title: 9/17: CBS Evening News
item.description: F-16 fighter jet crashes in Michigan; Latest on Trump-Kennedy Center drama.

item.title: Body of last missing hiker found after Grand Canyon flooding
item.description: Human remains found in the Grand Canyon this week have been identified as Timothy Allen Smith, the last person missing after deadly flash flooding in late August.

item.title: Grand Teton park forced to kill bear due to visitors' "poor decisions"
item.description: A black bear was euthanized in Grand Teton National Park after "poor decisions" made by human visitors, according to park officials.

item.title: Iran's proxies using Yemen to compound war's impact on oil prices
item.description: An attack on a Saudi Arabian pipeline and a simmering war between the Saudis and Iran's Houthi allies in Yemen are pushing oil prices up.
